**1 of 4. Merge in order — each PR targets the one before it.**

Arbor's half of the boundary with Nucleos. Nothing here calls Nucleos yet; this is the shape of the call and the schema both sides generate from.

## Truncation is never silent

`ExtractionJob` gains `truncated` and `truncationReason`, surfaced in Review.

An extraction that fails is visible — the document is REJECTED and the reviewer is told. One that reads only *part* of a document is not: the fields look identical to a complete read, the reviewer confirms them, and that confirmation is what sets the provenance tier. A partial read would quietly produce a VERIFIED record backed by a document nobody read in full.

The notice fires on the flag alone. Inferring truncation from the reason string would let a job that recorded a reason without setting the flag pass silently.

## The contract

Seven JSON Schema payload shapes as the neutral source, generating TypeScript here and Pydantic on the Nucleos side, with a drift check and a committed digest. I confirmed the check fails on a hand-edited generated file rather than only passing.

The plan says "six payload shapes" and then names seven. The named list is the requirement; the count is wrong.

Constraints (`minItems`, `exclusiveMinimum`) become Pydantic `Field` arguments. They were being dropped, so the models accepted a declaration with no goods lines and a negative mass — **a contract that states a rule it doesn't enforce is worse than one that stays quiet, because a reader trusts it.** TypeScript can't express these, so enforcement is Python-side only; that asymmetry is deliberate and documented.

## Document → text, and the CBAM branch

Arbor had no text representation of a document at all — it sent bytes to the model and got fields back. Nucleos's contract carries text, so this adds the stage Arbor had skipped.

`document-text.ts` is an adapter seam because the OCR vendor is deliberately undecided. The default transcribes with the model (no new account, works today); Textract and Document AI fail loudly rather than pretending to work, and an unknown `OCR_ADAPTER` is rejected rather than silently falling back.

`extraction-client.ts` **fails closed**, unlike the brain clients. The brain is an enhancement; Nucleos is the only thing that turns a CBAM document into CBAM structure. Degrading would land a document in Review looking like a clean read of a document with no CBAM data in it — and the reviewer would confirm that emptiness.

## Review

- Is the CBAM-relevant document set right? `CUSTOMS_DECLARATION`, `SUPPLIER_INVOICE`, `CBAM_DECLARATION`, in one auditable place.
- `MAX_TRANSCRIBED_PAGES = 30` is a judgement call.

1436 tests pass, `tsc` clean.
